newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania amends foreign debt data.
newsitem.headline: Romania amends foreign debt data.

text.p: The Romanian government on Sunday amended figures on the country's medium- and long-term foreign debt, putting the sum at $6.9 billion instead of the previously announced $10.9 billion.

"Romania's foreign debt totals $6.9 billion," government spokesman Eugen Serbanescu said in response queries after a statement was issued from his office on Sunday clarifying data he gave at a news conference on Saturday night.
He did not say how the mix-up had occurred.
The figure of $10.9 billion represented "the total of state borrowings made until December 31, 1996, part of which was repaid and part still to be drawn by Romania", he said.
Romania has so far paid nearly $1.0 billion on loans made after the 1989 collapse of communism, Serbanescu said.
The figure of $6.9 billion compared with a total of $6.255 billion at the end of September, 1996.
The government has set foreign borrowings in 1997 at up to $3.2 billion to fund investments, economic restructuring and enhance Romania's hard currency reserves.

The country's central bank governor said last month that Romania's external debt limit would be about $3.0 billion this year, with BNR expected to raise medium- and long-term loans worth up to $1.5 billion from international markets.

Romania resumed syndicated loans in 1995, followed by its first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year. It got its first rating from major agencies -- a BB plus from Japan Credit Rating Agency, BB-minus by Standard and Poors and Britain's IBCA and BA-three by Moody's Investors Service.
The ratings were based, among other criteria, on a relatively low external debt level. -- Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
